correctness.rationale: For positive initial mean, the velocity is locally Lipschitz in the characteristic position and the two moments on m≥m₀/2; q∈[0,1] gives inward boundary velocities. Local characteristic iteration gives the probability evolution, and monotonicity of m extends it globally. Independently, differentiating q+m² gives the single integral ∫2(x+m)V dμ=∫(q−x²)dμ=0. Writing V=v/[2(x+m)]−(x−m)/2 gives m′=vG/2 and v′=−2mvG, so m≥m₀ and G≥1/2, giving variance decay and convergence to the stated Dirac mass in W₂. Jensen and x²≤x give the exact extremizers at each interior mean. The all-zero initial law is separately stationary by convention, and the empirical law proof uses the full-sum degree normalization, not leave-one-out or stochastic fixation. The independent unequal-mass example in python3 /workspace/independent_checks.py (section 2) verifies the neutral moment identities with L²=102497/264600; the characteristic/moment argument establishes the universal claims.
